questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Average kinetic energy of one molecule
questions.learningObjective: Explain why the mean kinetic energy of a molecule is the same in every gas
questions.stem: Why is the mean kinetic energy of a molecule of an ideal gas the same in every gas at a given temperature?

options.text: Because every gas at a given temperature holds the same number of molecules per volume
options.misconception: assumes equal number density for all gases

options.text: Because the walls of the container reflect the molecular energy back into the gas
options.misconception: credits the container walls with the shared energy

options.text: Because the collisions between molecules are perfectly elastic for every gas
options.misconception: invents perfect elasticity as the reason

options.text: Because the temperature measures the shared mean kinetic energy, whatever the molecular mass

questions.explanation: Temperature is defined through the mean kinetic energy per molecule, so it is the same for all ideal gases at that temperature. The other options each confuse the definition with a mechanism.
questions.hint: Ask what the temperature of a gas is measured by.
